name: Benaiah
bio:
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was placed over David's bodyguard, the Cherethites and Pelethites, as part of the royal administration David established once his kingdom was secure (2 Samuel 8:18), a position he still held after Sheba's revolt was crushed (2 Samuel 20:23).

Benaiah, a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, is remembered for extraordinary feats of his own: he struck down two of Moab's best warriors, climbed down into a pit to kill a lion on a snowy day, and killed a huge Egyptian warrior armed only with a club, wrestling the Egyptian's own spear from his hand and killing him with it. These exploits won him a name among the Three, David's most elite warriors, though he did not attain to the standing of the top three themselves; David set him over his personal guard (2 Samuel 23:20-23). When Adonijah tried to seize the throne as David lay dying, Benaiah remained loyal, answering David's plan to crown Solomon with a wholehearted "Amen," and escorted Solomon to his anointing at Gihon alongside Zadok and Nathan (1 Kings 1:32-38). In his final instructions, David specifically charged Solomon to deal with Joab's bloodguilt, and once Adonijah's second bid for the throne — requesting Abishag as his wife — revealed his continued ambition, Solomon sent Benaiah to strike him down. Benaiah also executed Joab, who had fled to the altar for sanctuary, and finally carried out Shimei's execution as well, becoming the instrument of Solomon's consolidation of power; Solomon then placed him over the army in Joab's place (1 Kings 2:25, 29-35, 46), a position he still held as Solomon organized his royal administration (1 Kings 4:4).
